Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build recorded in that item (SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, from https://build.stencil.so/d/omp/20261017-231446-291e055/omp-darwin-arm64), verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge or a ruleset or settings change, and never a stand-in, adjudication or backoff reset unless the owner names the PR and head (and the finding) in the current request after an Owner instruction comment. Never edit, delete, dismiss or minimise an oracle review, review comment or commit status, and never post a commit status by hand. Run /oracle-review only on a pending or absent head, or after a Dispute: reply with file:line counter-evidence; never to re-roll a decided head. Do not close, reopen, rerun or rebase other PRs. Until oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025 merges, publish only from the owner's Mac. Rollback: if a change to the verdict or gate workflows or to the local review breaks its first live run after merge in a way that blocks other PRs, stop, run make trunk-revert PR=<n>, and report to the owner, who chooses between an absence stand-in and the broken-oracle-gate procedure. Never print tokens, keys, or the gateway URL or hostname; never spend model quota outside the review harness. Owner decisions are recorded in context and in the decisions file; a step that would contradict one stops and asks the owner.

Original description follows.

Problem: oracle findings arrive only after a PR exists. Each NO-SHIP or SHIP WITH FIXES costs a new head and another full CI and oracle round of 2h or more at 2026-10-25 load; #3465 and #3472 each lost a round to a High finding that day, and authoring agents skipped the pre-publication self-review. A local review cannot count towards oracle-gate, because the author controls what is reviewed; it can catch findings before the PR exists.

Outcome (owner decisions 2026-10-25): make pr-open runs a local oracle review of the branch's diff against the merge base with origin/develop before it pushes or opens anything.
- Same machinery as CI: a local plan built from git (cli.py plan gains a local mode: base and head SHAs, no PR number, no prior reviews), the same TypeSafe classification, policy, reviewer selection, templates, harness and redaction, and the attempt-loop command from oracle-verdict-single-job-20261025. No second loop.
- Classifier key: TYPESAFE_API_KEY from the macOS keychain service TYPESAFE_API_KEY. When it is absent (including cloud sessions), use the fixed default: the policy's medium-bucket reviewer with the standard template, or the gate template when review-machinery files change, and print that the default was used.
- Credentials: local sessions use the oracle-local gateway client at http://127.0.0.1:4000 with ~/.omp/oracle-gateway/local-client.token; cloud builders use the oracle-cloud client over the tailnet from their environment (oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025).
- Blocking: Critical or High findings make pr-open refuse. A PR body line `Local oracle override: <non-empty reason>` lets the author proceed on a false positive; pr-open keeps the line in the body so the reason is visible on the PR.
- Failure mode: block until it can run. Gateway unreachable, timeout, quota exhaustion or reviewer absence makes pr-open refuse with the reason; the override line does not cover this case.
- Scope: it reviews the committed HEAD that pr-open will push, never uncommitted changes. A result is cached by patch digest, policy hash and harness version, so re-running pr-open on an unchanged patch reuses it instead of reviewing again.
- Output is labelled as a local advisory review that may differ from the CI oracle. It posts nothing to GitHub.

Decision gates:
1. Before editing, confirm that the attempt-loop command from oracle-verdict-single-job-20261025 can run without GitHub event inputs. If it cannot, extend it minimally in this item; never add a second loop.
2. Reverts are unaffected: make trunk-revert opens its PR with gh pr create directly (scripts/trunk_revert.py:339-356, Makefile trunk-revert target), not through make pr-open. Re-check before editing; if that has changed, stop and ask whether develop-recovery reverts skip the local review.
3. Harness version: the local review runs only when the installed omp matches the version CI's reviewers use (the pin in .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml); otherwise it cannot run and pr-open refuses with the version mismatch, under the block-until-it-can-run decision.
4. Concurrency: at most one local review at a time per machine (a file lock), because local reviews share gateway accounts and quota with CI reviews. If measured waits make pr-open impractical, record the numbers and ask the owner before raising the limit.

Item guardrails: no change to the CI oracle, oracle-gate, the policy or selection logic; the local result never counts as a verdict and is never posted; no token or key is printed or written to the repository; pushes after the PR exists are out of scope (they get the CI oracle).
